display_name: Re-check role ownership at act time
description: READ-ONLY act-time ownership re-check (role-model v4 §5.0): does the calling session STILL hold the named role right now? Given the role name and the caller's own agent_instance_id, it sources the caller's stable agent_session_id from that session's peer_binding row (never a caller-supplied id), reads the live role_binding holder, and returns holds=true only when the live holder's session id equals the caller's. Resolution is advisory and can go stale between resolve time and act time (another session may have displaced the holder); this verb is the pull-truth check a holder runs at the moment it performs a privileged act. It NEVER writes — do not 're-check' by re-claiming (peer_claim_role is a WRITE that would steal the role back from a legitimate new holder). It also reports delivery_route_attached: whether the role's CURRENT holder still has a live bridge bound (an MCP session or an armed watcher), because a role binding is durable and outlives the session that claimed it. Primary use: Git-Controller's commit procedure Step 9.5, immediately before mutating git, confirms it still holds Git-Controller.
embedding_description: Confirm at act time that this session still owns a role before doing something privileged, reading only and writing nothing. Answers 'do I still hold Git-Controller, Coordinator, or Architect right now?' by comparing the live binding's holder against the caller. The ownership re-check that catches a displacement partway through a procedure.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: holds (True only when the live role_binding holder's stable agent_session_id equals the caller's — the caller still owns the role), name (the role), agent_session_id (the caller's stable session id resolved from its peer_binding; empty when the session exported no carrier), and delivery_route_attached (True when the role's CURRENT holder — whoever that is — has an open bridge bound, i.e. a live MCP session or an armed watcher). holds=False means the role is vacant OR held by a different session — do NOT act on the role's authority. delivery_route_attached is about the holder's receive path, not the caller's ownership: it is False for a vacant role and False for a holder whose session is gone, and it does not promise a wake will fire, only that a route is currently bound.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Surface the boolean plainly: True → the caller still holds the role and may proceed with the privileged act; False → STOP, the role moved (or the caller never held it). The operator-facing identifier is the role name. Report delivery_route_attached separately and never as a synonym for holds: holds=True with delivery_route_attached=False is the normal reading of a claim that has outlived its receiver.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: On holds=True, proceed with the gated act. On holds=False, do NOT re-claim to 'fix' it (that steals the role) — stop and report that ownership moved. When routing work to a role and delivery_route_attached is False, expect the message to be persisted rather than delivered live, and say so instead of assuming it was received.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Read-only §5.0 act-time ownership re-check. Sources the caller's stable agent_session_id from its own peer_binding row (by agent_instance_id), then compares it to the live role_binding holder via the store-level holds_role. No writes, no address book.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: missing_argument: 'name' or 'agent_instance_id' was empty. state_service_unavailable: the state_service is not bound on this solet.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: missing_argument: pass a non-empty role name and the caller's own agent_instance_id (from its peer_register response). state_service_unavailable: bind the state_service (postgres_state_management_plugin) in service_bindings.json and restart.
